title: Solving nonlinear programs with Uno
text: Uno wraps Uno C++ solver (Unifying Nonlinear Optimization) C API. describe nonlinear program R callbacks — objective, gradient, constraints, Jacobian Lagrangian Hessian — Uno solves . package R analog unopy Python binding, intended nonlinear (DNLP) solver backend CVXR. Two solver paths available box: filtersqp SQP preset, whose QP subproblems solved HiGHS (built source package); ipopt interior-point preset, whose symmetric-indefinite KKT systems solved MUMPS, reached run time rmumps package.

title: Solving nonlinear programs with Uno
text: solve Hock–Schittkowski problem 15, canonical test used Uno’s example: minx100(x2−x12)2+(1−x1)2s.t.x1x2≥1,x1+x22≥0,x1≤0.5. \min_{x}\; 100\,(x_2 - x_1^2)^2 + (1 - x_1)^2 \quad\text{s.t.}\quad x_1 x_2 \ge 1,\; x_1 + x_2^2 \ge 0,\; x_1 \le 0.5 .  solution x⋆=(0.5,2)x^\star = (0.5,\,2) objective 306.5306.5.

title: Solving nonlinear programs with Uno
text:
Jacobian Hessian supplied COO (coordinate) form: give sparsity pattern row/column index vectors , callback returns nonzero values point. Indices 0-based (base_indexing = 0L). Hessian lower triangle Lagrangian σ∇2f+∑iλi∇2ci\sigma\,
abla^2 f + \sum_i \lambda_i 
abla^2 c_i. default Uno uses negative Lagrangian convention, L=σf−y⊤cL = \sigma f - y^	op c – Hessian subtracts lambda terms. Hessian instead returns σ∇2f+∑iλi∇2gi\sigma
abla^2 f + \sum_i \lambda_i 
abla^2 g_i (convention used IPOPT CVXR’s sparsediff oracle), pass lagrangian_sign = "positive" constraint-Hessian terms get right sign. linear constraints constraint Hessian zero choice matter.
code: objective <- function(x) 100 * (x[2] - x[1]^2)^2 + (1 - x[1])^2 gradient  <- function(x) c(400 * x[1]^3 - 400 * x[1] * x[2] + 2 * x[1] - 2,                            200 * (x[2] - x[1]^2)) constraints <- function(x) c(x[1] * x[2], x[1] + x[2]^2)  # Jacobian nonzeros at (rows, cols) = {(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)} (0-based) jacobian <- function(x) c(x[2], 1, x[1], 2 * x[2])  # lower-triangular Lagrangian Hessian nonzeros at {(0,0),(1,0),(1,1)} hessian <- function(x, sigma, lambda)   c(sigma * (1200 * x[1]^2 - 400 * x[2] + 2),     -400 * sigma * x[1] - lambda[1],     200 * sigma - 2 * lambda[2])

title: Solving nonlinear programs with Uno
text: ipopt preset uses MUMPS linear solver. pass options = list(logger = "SILENT") keep Uno quiet (see Solver options ). optimization_status (solution_status) returned named integers – value Uno’s enum code name canonical label. Use names() label [[1]] bare code (recall x[1] keeps name, x[[1]] drops ): result also carries dual solution set diagnostic counters:
code: res <- uno_solve(   n = 2L, lb = c(-Inf, -Inf), ub = c(0.5, Inf), sense = "minimize",   obj = objective, grad = gradient,   m = 2L, cl = c(1, 0), cu = c(Inf, Inf), cons = constraints,   jac_rows = c(0L, 1L, 0L, 1L), jac_cols = c(0L, 0L, 1L, 1L), jac = jacobian,   hess_rows = c(0L, 1L, 1L), hess_cols = c(0L, 0L, 1L), hess = hessian,   x0 = c(-2, 1), preset = "ipopt", base_indexing = 0L, verbose = FALSE,   options = list(logger = "SILENT") )  res$optimization_status   # named integer: c(SUCCESS = 0L) #> SUCCESS  #>       0 res$objective             # 306.5 #> [1] 306.5 res$primal                # (0.5, 2) #> [1] 0.5 2.0 names(res$optimization_status)   # "SUCCESS" #> [1] "SUCCESS" res$optimization_status[[1L]]    # 0L #> [1] 0 res$constraint_dual #> [1] 7.000000e+02 5.568458e-10 res$iterations #> [1] 18 res$objective_evaluations #> [1] 22 res$cpu_time #> [1] 0.020043

title: Solving nonlinear programs with Uno
text: Beyond preset, Uno solver option can passed options named list; values coerced option’s declared type, options applied preset override . useful ones: unknown option name, value option rejects, raises error rather silently ignored.
code: # cap the iteration count uno_solve(..., preset = "ipopt", options = list(max_iterations = 50L))  # pick the linear solver explicitly, and silence output uno_solve(..., preset = "ipopt",           options = list(linear_solver = "MUMPS", logger = "SILENT"))

title: Solving nonlinear programs with Uno
text: convex problems — smooth problems produced CVXR’s DNLP reduction — filtersqp (HiGHS) ipopt (MUMPS) work, explicit Hessian must supplied (HiGHS use L-BFGS approximation). nonconvex problems like HS015, SQP subproblems indefinite; HiGHS solve , use interior-point ipopt preset (handles indefiniteness inertia correction MUMPS), .

title: R Interface to the Uno Nonlinear Optimization Solver
text: Hock–Schittkowski problem 15 (x* = (0.5, 2), f* = 306.5), solved interior-point preset. Derivatives supplied COO form (0-based indices); Hessian lower triangle Lagrangian. Uno solver option can passed options named list (applied preset). See vignette("Uno") full walk-.
code: library(Uno)  objective   <- function(x) 100 * (x[2] - x[1]^2)^2 + (1 - x[1])^2 gradient    <- function(x) c(400 * x[1]^3 - 400 * x[1] * x[2] + 2 * x[1] - 2,                              200 * (x[2] - x[1]^2)) constraints <- function(x) c(x[1] * x[2], x[1] + x[2]^2) jacobian    <- function(x) c(x[2], 1, x[1], 2 * x[2]) hessian     <- function(x, sigma, lambda)   c(sigma * (1200 * x[1]^2 - 400 * x[2] + 2),     -400 * sigma * x[1] - lambda[1],     200 * sigma - 2 * lambda[2])  res <- uno_solve(   n = 2L, lb = c(-Inf, -Inf), ub = c(0.5, Inf), sense = "minimize",   obj = objective, grad = gradient,   m = 2L, cl = c(1, 0), cu = c(Inf, Inf), cons = constraints,   jac_rows = c(0L, 1L, 0L, 1L), jac_cols = c(0L, 0L, 1L, 1L), jac = jacobian,   hess_rows = c(0L, 1L, 1L), hess_cols = c(0L, 0L, 1L), hess = hessian,   x0 = c(-2, 1), preset = "ipopt", base_indexing = 0L, verbose = FALSE,   options = list(logger = "SILENT") )  res$objective   # 306.5 res$primal      # 0.5 2

title: Solve a nonlinear program with Uno — uno_solve
code: uno_solve(   n,   lb,   ub,   sense,   obj,   grad,   m,   cl,   cu,   cons,   jac_rows,   jac_cols,   jac,   hess_rows,   hess_cols,   hess,   x0,   preset,   base_indexing,   verbose,   options = list(),   lagrangian_sign = c("negative", "positive"),   dual0 = NULL,   iter_callback = NULL,   log_callback = NULL )

title: Solve a nonlinear program with Uno — uno_solve
text: n number variables. lb, ub variable lower/upper bounds (length `n`; use `-Inf`/`Inf`). sense `"minimize"` `"maximize"`. obj, grad objective `function(x)` gradient `function(x)`. m number constraints (0 unconstrained). cl, cu constraint lower/upper bounds (length `m`). cons constraint `function(x)` returning length-`m` vector. jac_rows, jac_cols COO row/column indices Jacobian nonzeros. jac Jacobian `function(x)` returning nonzero values. hess_rows, hess_cols COO indices lower-triangular Hessian. hess Lagrangian Hessian `function(x, sigma, lambda)` returning lower-triangular nonzero values, `NULL` (Uno uses L-BFGS approximation, HiGHS subproblem solver use). x0 initial primal iterate (length `n`). preset Uno preset, e.g. `"filtersqp"` (SQP) `"ipopt"` (interior point, using MUMPS linear solver). base_indexing 0 C-style 1 Fortran-style COO indices. verbose `FALSE`, suppress Uno's solution printout. options named list Uno solver options applied preset (override ), e.g. `list(max_iterations = 200L, tolerance = 1e-8, linear_solver = "MUMPS")`. value coerced option's declared Uno type; unknown option name unacceptable value raises error. lagrangian_sign Lagrangian multiplier sign convention `hess` callback uses: `"positive"` \(L = \sigma f + y^\top c\) (standard convention used IPOPT sparsediff oracle) `"negative"` \(L = \sigma f - y^\top c\). Defaults `"negative"`, matching Uno's C-API default. **Must match convention `hess` returns**, otherwise Lagrangian Hessian's constraint terms get wrong sign (invisible constraints linear, since Hessian zero). dual0 optional warm-start dual iterate, `NULL` (Uno's default). iter_callback optional `function(info)` called acceptable iterate; return `TRUE` terminate solve early. `info` named list `primals`, `lower_bound_dual`, `upper_bound_dual`, `constraint_dual`, `objective_multiplier`, `primal_feasibility`/`stationarity`/ `complementarity` residuals. Errors callback caught treated "terminate". `NULL` disables . log_callback optional `function(text)` receives Uno's output stream chunks (sink solver log); `NULL` leaves output stdout. Independent `verbose` (controls much Uno prints).

title: Solve a nonlinear program with Uno — uno_solve
text: named list. `optimization_status` `solution_status`   **named integers** form `c(SUCCESS = 0L)`: value Uno's enum   code name canonical label, can key status map   `names(status)` still read code (e.g. `status[[1L]]`). list   also holds objective, primal dual solutions (`constraint_dual`,   `lower_bound_dual`, `upper_bound_dual`), KKT residuals, per-callback   evaluation counters.

title: Uno 2.7.3
text: Updated bundled Uno C++ solver upstream release 2.7.3. R-packaging patch set rebased onto v2.7.3; C API backward-compatible (binding unchanged). One internal fix: Uno 2.7.3 relocated Options::dump_default_options(), console output re-routed R-output mechanism (UNO_COUT) keep compiled library free raw std::cout CRAN compiled-code check. Added inst/COPYRIGHTS documenting copyright holders licenses bundled third-party libraries: Uno C++ solver HiGHS, including components HiGHS bundles (AMD, METIS, pdqsort, zstr, rcm, filereaderlp, Catch2, CLI11). permissive MIT-compatible (MIT / BSD-3-Clause / Apache-2.0 / zlib / Boost Software License 1.0); none copyleft. Copyright: file inst/COPYRIGHTS field cph entry HiGHS development team record package metadata. file lives inst/, attribution survives installation. MUMPS (reached run time GPL-licensed rmumps package) BQPD bundled.
